analysis.title: CIO Views – Weekly Bulletin, Week 44: US elections and US payrolls – what to watch for
key_insights: Eastspring will watch two things in the Nov 3 US mid-term results: voter support for candidates and local ballot measures that would restrict data center development, and the success of Progressive candidates and initiatives.

The US AI infrastructure boom is described as crucial for Asian export and earnings growth over the next several years. Eastspring says political constraints on data center development are increasingly important, beyond the profitability and financing-cost worries that have dominated AI capex anxiety.

Polling shows broad opposition to data centers. Politico/PF Global found over 50% oppose data center development within three miles of their homes. ABC News/Ipsos in October found 66% oppose building new data centers in the US and 72% oppose one in their local community.

Races where data center policy is a campaign issue: Ohio (Brown vs Husted for Senate, Acton vs Ramaswamy for governor, 21 local data center proposals), Michigan (7th district and Senate El-Sayed vs Rodgers), Texas (Talarico vs Paxton for Senate, Hinojosa vs Abbott for governor), Georgia (Ossoff vs Collins), Arizona 1st district (Feely vs Shah), New Mexico governor (Haaland vs Hull).
A broadly Democratic-leaning Congress would likely block Republican federal pre-emption laws that would override local or state data center moratoriums.

A wave of Progressive victories could raise the risk of tax increases on the very wealthy and on corporations after the 2028 Presidential election. California's Proposition 40 (the billionaire tax) is the key measure to watch.

Eastspring links the Progressive outcome to the US equity outlook through the fall in labour income as a share of GDP since 2000 and the rise of corporate profit as a share of GDP to new highs. Cited causes are China's WTO entry, automation, M&A concentration and declining union membership.

The mid-terms are unlikely to change the tariff or geopolitical landscape. Restricting presidential tariff or military powers would need a 2/3 majority in both houses to override a veto, and no credible polls or probability markets point to a Democratic 2/3 Senate majority.

For Friday's US payrolls, Eastspring will focus on wage growth over job growth. Collapsed immigration limits labour force growth and job gains, so the unemployment rate and especially wage growth are the main signals of labour market tightness for the Fed.

The Q3 Employment Cost Index, released last Friday, showed labour compensation growth slowed further despite unemployment and underemployment at levels historically seen as full employment. Eastspring says this lowers inflation risk and the pressure on the Fed to raise rates.
Eastspring expects the Fed to raise the Fed Funds rate by 25bps in December. The market is pricing a further 25bps hike, which depends on wage growth staying non-inflationary.
Eastspring's analysis says average hourly earnings growth must rise from the recent 0.2% m/m average to at least 0.3% m/m, more likely 0.4% m/m, to support current market pricing for Fed hikes.

Weekly market review: MSCI AC World -0.3%, S&P 500 -0.6%, Nasdaq -2.0%, Emerging Markets -0.7%, Asia Pacific ex Japan +0.6%, Japan -0.3%, gold -2.5%, dollar index +0.1%. Global corporate bonds and global high yield each +0.4%, global government bonds +0.3%.

Market data as of Oct 30, 2026: US 10-year Treasury yield 4.93%, S&P 500 7,580.07, Nasdaq Composite 25,437.00, Nikkei 225 63,290.11, KOSPI 5,730.74 (+3.25% on the week, -16.19% over a month), Jakarta Composite 5,057.05 (-7.03% on the week, -41.52% YTD), Shanghai Composite -2.48% on the week.

risk_factors: Voter and local ballot support for data center restrictions could constrain the US AI infrastructure build-out that Asian exports and earnings depend on.

A wave of Progressive election wins could raise the risk of higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations after the 2028 Presidential election, with California's Proposition 40 (billionaire tax) as a marker.
If wage growth stays near 0.2% m/m, the further Fed hike priced by the market may not be justified.
Reduced immigration constrains labour force growth and job gains.
geopolitical: Eastspring says the US mid-terms are unlikely to change the tariff or geopolitical landscape, since Congress would need a 2/3 majority in both houses to override a veto on bills restricting presidential tariff or military authority.
Michigan Senate race between El-Sayed and Rodgers is clouded by issues of religion and positions relating to Israel and Palestine.

tension_points.theme: Fed hike pricing vs wage growth
tension_points.bull_case: Hot wage growth at 0.3-0.4% m/m would support the further 25bps Fed hike the market prices beyond the December hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Q3 Employment Cost Index showed slowing labour compensation growth despite full-employment-level unemployment, which lowers inflation risk and Fed hike pressure. Average hourly earnings recently ran 0.2% m/m.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Average hourly earnings growth in Friday's payrolls staying near 0.2% m/m instead of rising to at least 0.3% m/m would undercut the further hike priced by the market.
